title: The Substrate Cycle

sourceEvidence.locator: two linked novels imagine a civilization
sourceEvidence.excerpt: two linked novels imagine a civilization in which automated provisioning has made conventional money largely obsolete. Pando and the later Lattice can route essentials, coordinate fabrication, and maintain a universal material floor without prices. Scarcity persists in forms that cannot be manufactured cheaply: attention, singular land, ecological capacity, secrecy, political access, and permission to impose irreversible risk. Influence accrues through kratons, a reputation-like measure awarded

hook: Food and housing are guaranteed, but the right to reshape the world is still scarce.
readerPromise: These stories make abundance feel rich with possibility and full of unfinished political choices. Enter a civilization where the most valuable thing to own may be the conditions of someone else’s future.
protectedRevelations: Rust Bloom, child-specific revelations, emergencies and Quito settlement
